claims.label: suggestion (non-blocking)
claims.subject: This new `crud.GetAll[models.District]` has no `.Limit()`, so it materializes every district in the country including the ineligible ones it then discards in memory — push the eligibility predicates into the query, or page it.
claims.discussion: This new `crud.GetAll[models.District]` has no `.Limit()`, so it materializes every district in the country including the ineligible ones it then discards in memory — push the eligibility predicates into the query, or page it. Introduced by this change. Before this diff the district-side read was `crud.GetMulti[models.District]` over keys derived from the admin UDIs that had already been found (removed at old line 1753), so it was bounded by the admin-UDI set; now it is bounded only by how many District entities exist with that country_code, and the eligibility filter runs afterwards in memory at lines 1862-1874. District is a wide model (61 `datastore:` properties in services/districts/models/district.go) and the whole entity is loaded, not a projection. The predicates being filtered in memory are stored, indexable properties — `District.EligibleForKADEmails()` at services/districts/models/district.go:451 is just `SendKADEmails() && m.RosterSyncingEnabled` over `dont_send_kad_emails`/`roster_syncing_enabled`, and `IsTest` is `is_test` — so adding them as equality filters on the query (and the matching index.yaml entry), or paging with `.Limit()` plus a cursor and handling one page per invocation, would bound the read. I traced both callers (monthly_admin_email_batch.go:444 and kad_email_subscriptions.go:529) and neither is in a transaction and neither bounds the result before this point, so nothing upstream or downstream caps it.
claims.failure_scenario: A monthly run for countryCode "US" calls getEmailableDistrictsByCountry, which GetAlls every District entity with country_code="US" into one slice with no .Limit() — including test districts, KAD-email-opted-out districts, roster-syncing-disabled districts, and districts with zero admin UDIs — so the job's peak memory grows with the total rostered district count rather than with the set it actually emails, and at 100x today's district count the Cloud Run instance OOMs with no GOMEMLIMIT backstop.

claims.label: suggestion (non-blocking)
claims.subject: getEmailableDistrictsByCountry still loads every district in the country and filters is_test / roster-syncing in Go; both are indexed properties, so push them into the query too.
claims.discussion:
getEmailableDistrictsByCountry still loads every district in the country and filters is_test / roster-syncing in Go; both are indexed properties, so push them into the query too. The PR's rationale is to stop loading a broad set and filtering it down afterward, and the UDI half of the function now does exactly that. The district half does not: the query at line 1855-1856 filters on country_code alone, and lines 1863-1871 then drop districts on `d.IsTest != testDistrictsOnly` and `d.EligibleForKADEmails()` in memory.

Two of the three district predicates are indexed datastore properties and could move into the query. In services/districts/models/district.go: line 114 is `IsTest bool `datastore:"is_test"`` and line 143 is `RosterSyncingEnabled bool `datastore:"roster_syncing_enabled"`` — neither carries `,noindex`. The third, `DontSendKADEmails` (line 92), is `datastore:"dont_send_kad_emails,noindex"`, so that one genuinely has to stay an in-memory check; `EligibleForKADEmails()` is `SendKADEmails() && RosterSyncingEnabled` (district.go:451).

This matters more than a normal load-less nit because the emailable district count is now the function's latency driver, not just its memory cost: `len(districts)` feeds `datastore.BatchFilterIn(query, "district", districtKeys)` at line 1807, which chunks by 30 (pkg/gcloud/datastore/query.go:444), and those `ceil(D/30)` queries run through a 10-slot semaphore at lines 1810-1811 — so wall-clock grows as `D/300` roundtrip waves. The comment at 1800-1804 acknowledges the batching tradeoff in the abstract but the code leaves D at "all districts in the country" when two of the filters that shrink it are indexable.

These are equality filters only, which datastore serves by merging single-property indexes, so I do not believe this needs a new entry in services/districts/index.yaml — worth confirming against your local emulator run, since that is the one thing that would change the cost of the suggestion.
claims.failure_scenario: The district fetch stays a load-everything-then-filter-in-Go scan, and since its surviving count sets the number of 30-key IN batches, the new cost driver is left larger than it needs to be — most visibly on the testDistrictsOnly=true path, which loads every non-test district in the country to keep a handful.
claims.suggestion: In getEmailableDistrictsByCountry, build the query as `datastore.NewQuery(models.DistrictKind).FilterField("country_code", "=", countryCode).FilterField("is_test", "=", testDistrictsOnly).FilterField("roster_syncing_enabled", "=", true)`, and keep only the `d.SendKADEmails()` (DontSendKADEmails, noindex) check in the Go loop.

claims.subject: Rewritten kad_template-based email has no render test, unlike both of its siblings
claims.discussion: Rewritten kad_template-based email has no render test, unlike both of its siblings. Introduced by this change: both bodies are re-parented onto `emails/kad_template` and rewritten wholesale, but nothing renders them. The only HIPR test is `TestSendHIPRTeacherActivationEmail` (services/districts/rostering/emails_test.go:215), which goes through `emails.MockClient` and asserts only `Templates.TemplatePath() == "emails/hipr_teacher_activation_email"` — it never parses or executes the template, so it passes even if the template is broken. The two other district emails built on this same layout do have end-to-end tests that read the file from disk and push it through `prepareHTMLEmail` / the text equivalent: services/emails/serviceproviders/kad_template_test.go:115 and :256 (HTML) and :492 and :606 (text). The preview path (`CreateHIPRTeacherActivationEmailPreview`, services/districts/rostering/emails.go:582) is likewise mock-backed in tests, so it adds no coverage either. Because these templates are parsed and executed only at send time, a `{{define}}`/arity/funcmap mistake in either file would surface as a failed activation email for every KAD-trial teacher, not as a red build. Adding a `hipr_teacher_activation_email` case alongside the existing suite in kad_template_test.go (one HTML, one text) would cover the parse, the subject, and the presence of the confirm-account URL for roughly the cost of the sibling tests.
claims.failure_scenario: A typo in either template (e.g. a mistyped param name in the `{{i18n "%(stepLabel)s..."}}` call at gohtml:67, or an unbalanced `{{define}}`) ships green: `make tesc` passes because no test executes these files. At send time `prepareHTMLEmail` returns an error, `SendEmail` fails, and every teacher a district admin adds to a KAD trial never receives their activation email — the one message that contains the account-confirmation link.

claims.label: issue (blocking)
claims.subject: An empty `classrooms` list makes every error path return a success-looking response
claims.discussion:
An empty `classrooms` list makes every error path return a success-looking response. `_mapErrorToAllClassrooms` reports errors by writing into `result.Errors`, which `mapCreateWritingCoachAssignmentInputGraphQLToResponseGraphQL` sizes as `make([]*graphql.WritingCoachConfigError, len(assignmentInput.Classrooms))` (line 464). When the client sends `classrooms: []`, that slice has length zero, so this loop body never executes and the mutation returns `{classrooms: [], errors: []}` with a nil Go error — indistinguishable from success.

An empty list is a legal value for `classrooms: [WritingCoachConfigInputClassroom!]!`: the non-null markers constrain the list and its elements, not its length, so gqlgen accepts `[]` and the resolver runs. I grepped `services/humanities/` for any `len(...Classrooms) == 0` guard or equivalent and found none, and read the full resolver plus `writing_coach_config.graphql` — nothing caps or floors the list length at any layer.

That means all three failure paths added by this change go silent for an empty list: the `RequestUser` failure (line 157), the `IsLoggedIn` failure (line 164), and the `InvalidInput` mapping failure (line 177). The unauthorized case is the notable one — a caller who is not permitted to create assignments gets an HTTP 200 with no error at all. This is introduced by this change; the previous code was a stub that returned empty slices unconditionally, so there was no error contract to violate yet.

The root cause is that one slice serves two purposes: per-classroom results and whole-request errors. This is the part of the design the PR description is asking about. Making the whole-request error independent of the input length fixes the symptom; the more thorough fix is a separate top-level error field, since a config-level validation failure is not per-classroom at all (see the related finding on error-code collapse).
claims.failure_scenario: An empty `classrooms` list makes every error path return a success-looking response

claims.label: issue (blocking, best-practice)
claims.subject: ADR-303: `_mapErrorToAllClassrooms` populates no error when `classrooms` is empty, so every failure path returns a success-shaped result.
claims.discussion:
ADR-303: `_mapErrorToAllClassrooms` populates no error when `classrooms` is empty, so every failure path returns a success-shaped result. The add-graphql-mutation skill states the ADR-303 contract: "The resolver never returns a GraphQL-level error for a business failure; it returns a result object whose `error` field is populated."

Every failure path in the new resolver funnels through `_mapErrorToAllClassrooms`, whose entire body is a loop over the pre-sized error slice:

```go
476| 	for i := range result.Errors {
```

That slice is sized from the request: `464| errors := make([]*graphql.WritingCoachConfigError, len(assignmentInput.Classrooms))`. When `classrooms` is empty the loop body never runs and the helper returns a result whose `errors` list is empty — the error field is not populated.

I checked whether an empty list is reachable: the schema declares `classrooms: [WritingCoachConfigInputClassroom!]!` (`services/humanities/writing_coach_config.graphql:129`) — the list is non-null but may be empty — and grepping `Classrooms` across `services/humanities/resolvers/writing_coach_config.go` and `services/humanities/writing_coach_config/create_writing_coach_assignments.go` turns up no length/emptiness validation anywhere. So an unauthenticated request with `classrooms: []` reaches line 157 and returns an error-free result.

Fix: have the helper fall back to a single top-level error entry when there are no classrooms to attach one to (or reject an empty `classrooms` list as `INVALID_INPUT` before the response struct is built).
claims.failure_scenario: A logged-out (or phantom) caller — or one sending an invalid config — who passes `classrooms: []` gets back `{classrooms: [], errors: []}`, which is byte-identical to a successful no-op, so the client silently treats a rejected mutation as a success.

proposals.evidence: for i := range result.Errors at line 476 in _mapErrorToAllClassrooms never executes when classrooms is empty, so every failure path returns {errors: []} identical to success

Nothing fails when a new decrypting field is added, which is the exact drift the comment warns about. Introduced by this change. The comment states the failure mode precisely — "A decrypting field missing here silently loses the preload" — but no test enforces it. `TestEncryptedFieldsAreSchemaFields` checks only one direction (every listed name is a real schema field); the direction that actually rots is the other one. claims.label: issue (blocking)
claims.subject: Per-classroom `debugMessage` sends the raw, unredacted internal error to the client
claims.discussion: Per-classroom `debugMessage` sends the raw, unredacted internal error to the client. `assignment.Error.Error()` puts the full internal error string — message chain plus the wrapped `errors.Fields`/`log.Fields` extras — onto `WritingCoachConfigError.debugMessage`, which is a `@consumer(name: LANG_LIT)` field returned to the browser. Every other error path in this same service goes through automap, and automap builds that field as `errors.ErrorPresenter(ctx, err, true /* redactErrors */).Message` (`services/humanities/generated/automap/automap.go:41-46`); `pkg/lib/errors/graphql_presenter.go:34-52` shows exactly what the `redactErrors` branch buys you — it keeps only the human `message` of each wrapped `khanError` and drops the extras and the stack, whereas the non-redacted branch is `kaError.Error() + StackTrace(...)`. So this line deliberately ships the shape redaction exists to suppress. The errors that reach it are real internal ones: datastore failures from `PutWritingCoachConfig`, and `errors.Internal("createPlatformAssignment error", log.Fields{"errorCode": ...})` from `services/humanities/cross_service/assignments.go`. Introduced by this change. Note that none of the new tests select `debugMessage`, so the leak is invisible to the suite.
claims.failure_scenario: A teacher submits `createWritingCoachAssignments` and one classroom's datastore write fails; the mutation returns HTTP 200 with `errors[i].debugMessage` containing the raw khanError chain and its wrapped fields (datastore/entity internals, the downstream error code) straight to the browser, instead of the redacted message every other mutation in this service returns.

claims.label: issue (blocking, best-practice)
claims.subject: ADR-303/automap: `debugMessage` is filled with the raw `err.Error()` string, bypassing the `ErrorPresenter` redaction automap applies.
claims.discussion:
ADR-303/automap: `debugMessage` is filled with the raw `err.Error()` string, bypassing the `ErrorPresenter` redaction automap applies. The added line is:

```go
debug := assignment.Error.Error()
```

and it is assigned straight to the client-visible `DebugMessage` on the next lines.

`.claude/skills/add-graphql-mutation/references/automap-deep-dive.md` states the contract for this field: "**`debugMessage`:** if (and only if) the error type declares a `debugMessage: String` field, automap fills it with `errors.ErrorPresenter(ctx, err, true /* redactErrors */)` — a message redacted for end users." `.claude/skills/error-handling/references/resolvers.md` says what that redaction buys: "**End-user requests (redacted):** only the human-readable **messages** survive. The presenter walks the wrap chain, pulls each khanError's `message`, and joins them with `" > "`. The kind, the `errors.Fields{}`, internal function names, and the stack trace are all stripped."

What I checked: the sibling generated helper `services/humanities/generated/automap/automap.go` does exactly the documented thing — `msg := errors.ErrorPresenter(ctx, err, true /* redactErrors */).Message`. And `pkg/lib/errors/errors.go:245` documents `khanError.Error()` as the opposite: "We expose all metadata (except some special empty fields) about the error here" — its body writes `e.source`, the kind, and every sorted `extra` field. The errors that land here are constructed with fields: `services/humanities/cross_service/assignments.go` returns `errors.Internal("createPlatformAssignment error", log.Fields{"errorCode": ...})`, so that field value plus the internal source string is what reaches the client.

Fix: run it through the presenter, the way automap does.

claims.label: issue (blocking)
claims.subject: Attempts that can never be warmed are re-classified as cold and re-migrated on every single request
claims.discussion:
Attempts that can never be warmed are re-classified as cold and re-migrated on every single request. Introduced by this change. The classification switch treats "cold" as `default` — i.e. anything that is neither (`WordPair != "" && type matches`) nor (`type set && type differs`). Two categories fall into `default` permanently, so the lazy migration never converges for them:

1. **Challenge missing.** Lines 310-313 skip an attempt whose challenge was deleted or archived and leave it cold by design. On the next request that attempt is `default` again, so its key is re-added to the `GetMulti` at line 298 — forever, once per render.
2. **Legitimately empty pair.** An attempt whose `ChallengeType` *equals* `challengeType` but whose `WordPair` is `""` fails case 1 (empty pair) and fails case 2 (types are equal), so it lands in `default`. The backfill then writes it back with `WordPair = ""` (line 316/325) and the next request classifies it as cold again — and this one costs a `PutMulti` write, not just a read, on every render. This is not hypothetical: the doc comment the PR adds at `models/langlit_challenge.go:309-312` states outright that "a challenge with no IncorrectForm token legitimately yields ''".

I checked whether case 2 is reachable for freshly generated content: `isValidDependencyOutput` (`langlit_challenge_component.go:536-542`) does require at least one token with a non-empty `IncorrectForm`, so newly generated challenges are safe. That guard does not cover challenges written before it existed, nor the deleted-challenge path, which is unconditional.

Effect: a steady per-request datastore read (and, for category 2, write) amplification that the "improve in performance over time" story in the PR description assumes away. The fix is to make "already attempted migration" distinguishable from "never attempted" — e.g. treat `ChallengeType != ""` as warm regardless of `WordPair`, and record a sentinel (or skip re-queuing) for attempts whose challenge could not be hydrated.

claims.subject: Empty WordPair is used as the "needs migration" sentinel, but it is also a legitimate warm value, so those attempts never converge and are re-hydrated and re-written on every request.
claims.discussion:
Empty WordPair is used as the "needs migration" sentinel, but it is also a legitimate warm value, so those attempts never converge and are re-hydrated and re-written on every request. The switch at handlers.go:221-231 has three arms. An attempt with `ChallengeType == challengeType` and `WordPair == ""` fails arm 1 (`WordPair != ""`) and fails arm 2 (`ChallengeType != challengeType`), so it falls to `default` and is appended to `cold`. `_backfillLanglitAttempts` then hydrates the challenge and writes back `models.ExtractWordPair(challenge)`, which returns "" again (models/langlit_challenge.go:224-235 returns "" when no token carries an IncorrectForm) — the attempt is written with the exact same values and is cold again on the next request. The same holds for the `challenge == nil` branch at handlers.go:310-314, which deliberately leaves the attempt cold; `DeleteLanglitChallenge` exists at handlers.go:656, so deleted challenges are reachable.

This is doubled per request: `LanglitChallengeComponent` calls `ComputeProvenWordPairs` and then `ComputeSeenCorrectPairs`, and both run `_computeCorrectPairs` over the same slice. Warm attempts are deduped only because the first call mutates them in place — which is exactly what does not happen for this class.

The PR description's premise is "the data will be seamlessly upgraded and improve in performance over time". For this class it does the opposite: a permanent extra datastore read and an idempotent-but-repeated write on the student-facing challenge-fetch path, against a WrittenOnceModel. The models comment at langlit_challenge.go:308-312 already notes that "" is ambiguous; the code does not act on that.

claims.discussion:
Cold attempts whose challenge is missing (or yields an empty word pair) are never written back, so they re-hydrate on every request forever instead of migrating lazily as the description promises. The PR description states "the actual migration is done lazily... we never need to run an actual migration, because the data will be seamlessly upgraded and improve in performance over time." Two paths never reach that steady state.

1. In `_backfillLanglitAttempts`, when `challenge == nil` (line 310–313) the attempt is skipped with `continue`, so no key is appended to `putKeys`. Nothing marks the attempt as processed, so `_computeCorrectPairs` classifies it into the `default:` (cold) branch again on the next call and `GetMulti` re-fetches the missing key every time.

2. The `default:` branch at line 228 is also reached for a warm attempt whose `ChallengeType` matches but whose `WordPair` is `""`. `models.ExtractWordPair` returns `""` when no token carries an `IncorrectForm`, and the model comment you added on `WordPair` (langlit_challenge.go:309-312) explicitly acknowledges "a challenge with no IncorrectForm token legitimately yields ''". `isValidDependencyOutput` (entry_components/langlit_challenge_component.go:537-541) only guarantees this for newly generated challenges, not for ones cached before that validation existed. Such attempts are re-hydrated and re-written on every request.

A persisted "migration attempted" signal (e.g. writing `ChallengeType` alone, or a sentinel `WordPair`) would let both cases settle.

claims.label: issue (blocking, best-practice)
claims.subject: GraphQL schema: `progressFrom`/`progressUpTo` are deleted outright instead of `@deprecated`, which breaks already-shipped clients.
claims.discussion:
GraphQL schema: `progressFrom`/`progressUpTo` are deleted outright instead of `@deprecated`, which breaks already-shipped clients. The `add-graphql-field` skill states the rule directly: "**Additive is safe; changing what already ships is breaking.** Adding a field, query, type, input, or *output* enum value doesn't break existing clients. But **removing**, renaming, or retyping an existing field, **dropping an enum value**, or **tightening** an argument/nullability breaks already-shipped clients — the graph is federated, the gateway serves a persisted-query *safelist*, and the mobile floor is **8.4.1** (old app binaries can't be patched). The safe path is `@deprecated(reason: "…")` (keep serving it)".

This PR deletes rather than deprecates, in both the input and the output type — e.g. `"""The start date, if absent defaults to 'beginning of time'"""` / `    progressFrom: DateTime` from `input TeacherOverallProgressReportFilters`, and `    progressFrom: DateTime` / `    progressUpTo: DateTime` from `type TeacherOverallProgressReport`. The input-side removal is the sharper edge: an unknown input field is a validation error, so a stale client does not merely get a null field, its whole query is rejected.

What I checked on the checkout: `grep -rli teacherOverallProgressReport` finds only the `coaches` service as an in-repo consumer, and its regenerated `services/coaches/generated/genqlient/queries.go` hunk changes only a doc comment — it never selected these fields. The composed artifacts (`gengraphql/composed_schema.graphql`) were regenerated, so that part of the skill's checklist is satisfied. What I could not check from this repo is the web/mobile client side, which is exactly the population the rule is written to protect; the PR description's claim that "the filters aren't even wired up" covers the server-side plumbing, not whether a shipped operation still names the fields. If you have confirmed no persisted/safelisted operation and no ≥8.4.1 app build references them, say so on the PR and this is fine to land; otherwise mark the four fields `@deprecated(reason: "…")` now and delete them after the clients age out.
claims.failure_scenario: A shipped client (mobile floor 8.4.1, or a persisted web operation) that still sends `progressFrom`/`progressUpTo` in `TeacherOverallProgressReportFilters` or selects them on `TeacherOverallProgressReport` starts failing GraphQL validation the moment this deploys, blanking the whole classroom skills report for those users, and old app binaries cannot be patched.

claims.label: issue (blocking)
claims.subject: The same removal narrows the `TeacherOverallProgressReportFilters` input type, which rejects any shipped client that still sends `progressFrom`/`progressUpTo` in the filter.
claims.discussion:
Separate from the output-field removal: `progressFrom` and `progressUpTo` also disappear from `input TeacherOverallProgressReportFilters`, and the composed-schema hunk (@@ -78241,12 +78228,6 @@) carries that narrowing to the gateway. Removing an input field is breaking in the opposite direction from removing an output field — it breaks clients that *send* the value, not ones that read it, so a client can trip this even if it never selected `progressFrom` in its selection set.

The PR description says the filters "aren't even wired up," and that is true of the server: the resolver ignored the two values apart from echoing them back. But an ignored input field is still an *accepted* input field. Today a client sending `filters: {progressFrom: $from}` gets a successful (if unfiltered) response; after this change the same document fails validation outright.

The fix is the same shape as for the output fields — keep the two input fields, add `@deprecated(reason: "...")`, and drop them in a follow-up once no shipped operation sends them. That still gets you the dead code deleted from the resolver now.

The safe path is `@deprecated(reason: "…")` (keep serving it) or `@replaces(name: "…")` for a backward-compatible rename

claims.label: issue (blocking, best-practice)
claims.subject: Shared-code governance: production resolver suppresses `ka-import` to import `services/ai-guide` — use a cross-service query or copy the map instead.
claims.discussion:
Shared-code governance: production resolver suppresses `ka-import` to import `services/ai-guide` — use a cross-service query or copy the map instead. The added import is production code on a deployed request path (`queryResolver.GetAssessmentsLearnerInsights`), not a test or a script:

```go
"github.com/Khan/webapp/services/ai-guide/internal_reasoning/preprocessors" //nolint:ka-import // see above
```

`.claude/skills/shared-code-governance/SKILL.md` states the rule as non-negotiable: "**No service may import from another service.** Services talk to each other over GraphQL, never by importing each other's Go packages." and "When the linter flags a cross-service import in production code, the fix is never to suppress it — it's to choose the right tier from the decision tree above, or another sanctioned way across the boundary (a cross-service query, or copying with sync-tags). (Tests and scripts are the one tolerated exception.)" The reference file is explicit about which code may suppress: "The one tolerated exception is **non-production** code: test files (`*_test.go`) and command-line scripts (`cmd/*/main.go`) that aren't on any deployed request path… The test to apply: **if the code could ever run in production, don't suppress — share or copy it instead.**"

I checked the checkout: `grep -rn "ai-guide/internal_reasoning/preprocessors" --include=*.go services/assessments/` returns only the two import lines this PR adds, so no prior production precedent exists in `assessments` — the previous suppression lived in `cmd/fix_learner_insights/main.go`, which this PR deletes and which the skill explicitly tolerates as a script. The sanctioned options for the interim step are the ones the skill lists: a cross-service GraphQL query (which the PR description says is the eventual plan), or copying the small stable map into `assessments` wrapped in sync-tags so `code_syncing_lint.py` keeps the copies from drifting. That the suppression is temporary isn't one of the listed exceptions.

claims.discussion:
This trades a GraphQL field for a compile-time dependency from two production assessments resolvers on `services/ai-guide/internal_reasoning/preprocessors`, deepening the very coupling the PR removes; copy the skills map into assessments instead. The PR removes `name` from the ai-guide↔assessments wire, but replaces it with a stronger coupling in the opposite direction: `services/assessments/resolvers/get_or_create_learner_insights.go:22` and `services/assessments/resolvers/reporting/classroom_insights.go:22` now import an ai-guide *internal* package from GraphQL resolvers, suppressed with `//nolint:ka-import`.

`.claude/skills/shared-code-governance/references/crossing-import-boundaries.md` states the rule categorically: "For anything that ships to production, the answer is never `//nolint`" and "if the code could ever run in production, don't suppress — share or copy it instead"; the tolerated exception is only `*_test.go` and `cmd/*/main.go`. I grepped every non-test `nolint:ka-import` in the repo: all existing cross-service ones are `cmd/` scripts or dev tools (`content-editing/cmd/ai-translate-extracted-strings`, `districts/cmd/*`, `donations/cmd/*`, `ai-guide/cmd/user`); the rest are same-service `generated/graphql`. These two are the first cross-service imports on a deployed request path.

What makes the seam clearly wrong rather than merely irregular: after this PR, `GetSkillsForCode` has zero ai-guide callers. Grepping the symbol repo-wide returns only the two new assessments lines — ai-guide still uses `GetSubjectForCode`/`GetGradeLevelForCode`, but the `Skills` data now exists solely to serve assessments. So the map's `Skills` column belongs in assessments today, which is also what the PR description argues ("remove the map from ai-guide, where it doesn't belong"). The decision table's sanctioned move for a small, stable helper is copy it into assessments with sync-tags; alternatively, since the description says the names are already in the assessments DB, read them there now and skip the intermediate hack entirely.

I also checked the two things this could have broken and they are fine, so this is the only issue I'm raising: all nine codes in `mock_data/sample_insights.go` are present in the map (no name regressions from the removed hard-coded `Name`s), and the removed `name` field on the ai-guide types has no frontend consumer — grepping `*.ts/tsx/js/jsx/graphql` for `RollupDetailedSummaryResult` and `LearnerInsightsDetailedSummary` finds only the assessments schema's own retained type.
claims.failure_scenario: An ai-guide engineer edits or removes a `Skills` string in `StandardsToSkillsMap` (or renames `internal_reasoning/preprocessors` during the planned cleanup) with no signal that another service depends on it, and every teacher-facing assessments insight report silently shows a changed or empty `name` — or assessments simply stops compiling on an ai-guide-internal refactor.
